correction: Appended only explanatory Remarks and a fenced TikZ control-flow diagram; the complete original file is an unchanged prefix. All title/frontmatter, status, definitions, references and numbered algorithm text are byte-identical.

diagram_math_checks.objects: H is a d by d real Hessian, g and u_i are d-vectors, q_i are scalar sample cost offsets; x* is a displacement in R^d and theta_j is a candidate parameter.
diagram_math_checks.justification: Definition paragraphs preceding step 1 define every coefficient and U subset R^d. The diagram uses exactly these objects and does not assert an additional policy map or expected-cost relation.

diagram_math_checks.relation: The no branch of the symmetric-positive-definite H test returns no-step; its yes branch alone forms the QP.
diagram_math_checks.justification: Step 1 rejects nonsymmetric H or a nonzero x with x^T H x <= 0; the complement is precisely symmetric positive definiteness. Thus inversion in recovery occurs only after this gate.

diagram_math_checks.relation: QP feasible -> lexicographically least global maximizer -> sample search; QP infeasible -> recovery test.
diagram_math_checks.justification: Step 2 selects exactly this tie-broken maximizer in the feasible case. Its closed compact feasible set supports the choice; the independently read local well-definedness lemma proves compactness in step 1.1 and uniqueness of the tie rule in step 2.1.

diagram_math_checks.relation: In the infeasible branch, m=1 and u_1 != 0 -> v=H^{-1}u_1 and x*=-sqrt(2 delta/(u_1^T v)) v -> sample search. Otherwise return no-step.
diagram_math_checks.justification: Step 2 states this formula and these rejection cases. Symmetric positive definiteness gives invertibility and u_1^T H^{-1}u_1 > 0; local lemma step 2.2 derives this and explains that the recovery minimizer need not satisfy the infeasible cost constraint. The Remarks explicitly retain that limitation. An infeasible QP cannot occur with no cost constraints because x=0 satisfies the trust ellipsoid.

diagram_math_checks.relation: Both proposal paths enter the same ordered finite search; it first checks theta_j in U and only then empirical KL and all empirical cost inequalities. Passing outputs the first theta_j as theta_{k+1}; none passing returns no-step.
diagram_math_checks.justification: Definition step 3 fixes theta_j=theta_k+beta^j x*, j=0,...,L, these exact tests and the least passing index. Local lemma step 4.1 independently proves at most L+1 tests. No population-cost safety, exact-policy guarantee, improvement or convergence is asserted by this diagram.

diagram_math_checks.relation: All directed branches and terminal states match steps 1–3.
diagram_math_checks.justification: Native standalone view shows 11 boxes and 11 directed connections: two outgoing at H, two at QP feasibility, two at the recovery condition, one at QP formation, one from each proposal to search and two search exits. Three no-step terminals are deliberate copies of the same return. This directed control-flow graph has no cycle/closing-edge assertion, open/closed endpoints or crossing conventions.
